Check a results object against the contract

Source: R/check_results.R
check_results.Rd

check_results() checks a results object against the contract of save_results(). It reports each rule as PASS or FAIL, and it stops on nothing.

Usage

check_results(x)

Arguments

x

The results object, normally from read_results().

Value

A data.frame with one row per rule and the columns rule, status and detail. status is "PASS" or "FAIL".

Details

The rule element_names checks that the manifest is there. The rules manifest_scenario, manifest_data and manifest_source check that it is valid. The seven rules:

  • element_names: x is a list with the element manifest exactly once and at least one other element. The other element MAY be missing when manifest$analyses puts a kind in results_gitexclude.qs2. Each element has a name. Each name is syntactic, so make.names() does not change it, and no name is there twice.

  • exclusions_table: when x has an element exclusions, it is a data.frame with the columns step, n_before, n_excluded and n_after, and MAY have the column data. save_results() writes data for the exclusion table of a cohort. When manifest$stacked is TRUE, it also has the column sim that save_results() adds when it stacks. On every row, n_before - n_excluded == n_after. Without an element exclusions, the rule passes and says so.

  • allowed_objects: each element at each depth is one of these:

    • a data.frame, of any class that inherits from data.frame. This includes a data.table and a tibble.

    • an atomic vector of any length and of any class, including a matrix, an array, a factor, a Date and a POSIXct.

    • NULL.

    • a list of such elements, named or not. The list has no class, or only classes from this set: list, AsIs, table, noquote, difftime, Date, POSIXct, factor and integer64.

    Each other element fails, and the detail names its path, its class and a fix. This includes a function, an environment, an S4 object, an R6 object, a formula and each other list with a class. A fitted model of the class lm, glm, gam, merMod, brmsfit, coxph or lavaan fails too. The detail has a fix for a model, a formula, an htest, a POSIXlt, a package_version and an sf geometry. For each other object, convert it to a data.frame or a plain list.

    The walk goes into the columns of a data.frame, so a model in a list column fails too. It also goes into the attributes of each object, and it writes the path of an attribute as attr(x$a, "terms"). So the terms attribute of a model frame fails. The walk skips the attributes that R and data.table set: names, dim, dimnames, row.names, class, levels, tzone, units, comment, sorted, index and .internal.selfref.

  • no_row_per_person: no element at any depth of the results has one value for each row of the data. manifest$n_rows_data holds one row count, or one for each data element. For a cohort, manifest$n_rows_before_exclusions and manifest$n_rows_after_exclusions hold the rows before and after the exclusions too. manifest$n_rows_lists holds the rows of each data.frame of a data element that is a list of data.frames with 2 or more numbers of rows. For each count n of 2 or more in any of the four, the rule fails each of these:

    • a data.frame with n rows.

    • an atomic vector of length n, also a factor, a Date or a POSIXct.

    • a matrix or an array with a dimension n.

    The walk goes into lists, the columns and list columns of data.frames, and attributes. It does not go into manifest or exclusions. A count that is NA, 0 or 1 checks nothing, and a manifest$n_rows_data without another count checks nothing too. A table with fewer rows than the data passes, and so does a vector with one value for each group.

    For stacked results, the rule is about the rows of one simulation. It takes the results apart into the value of each simulation. It uses the column sim of each data.frame and the entries sim_<kkkk> of each other value. It checks each simulation against its own counts in manifest$n_rows_by_sim. So 400 simulations of a 1-row table, a stacked table of 400 rows, pass with 400 rows of data in each simulation. A table with one row for each person in one simulation fails. Stacked results without manifest$n_rows_by_sim get the rule of unstacked results. An older pbn wrote their counts as NA, so they check nothing.

  • manifest_scenario: manifest has the elements scenario, sim and sims, and scenario is one string.

  • manifest_data: manifest has exactly one of data_files and fake_md5. It has data_files when scenario is "real", and fake_md5 when scenario is another string. fake_md5 MUST be one string of 32 lower-case hex digits. data_files MUST be a data.frame with the columns file, size and mtime. Each file is a name that comes once, each size a number of 0 or more, and each mtime a number. It has 0 rows when the data folders have no file. A manifest with data_md5, the md5 of the data files of an older pbn, fails this rule: run the scenario again. For "real", manifest$fake_real_data MUST be TRUE or FALSE. A real manifest of an older pbn has no fake_real_data, so it fails this rule: run the scenario again.

    For "real", manifest$failed_fake_checks MUST be a character vector without attributes, also no names. It MAY be empty. Each element MUST match ^[a-z0-9_]+$, MUST NOT be NA or "real", and MUST come once. The element MUST be there when manifest$pbn_version is a version of 2026.11.25 or newer. A manifest without it and without such a version passes, as the results of an older pbn do.

  • manifest_source: manifest$source_md5 is a named character vector of md5 values, each a string of 32 lower-case hex digits. It names the run script <version>_run.R of manifest$version, or a vNN_run.R when the manifest has no valid version. A results file that pbn 2026.11.20 or older wrote has no source_md5, so it fails this rule.

check_results() checks the object of results.qs2 or of sim_<kkkk>.qs2. The object of a file of gitexclude MAY hold data for each person, and these rules do not apply to it. See the section Two files of save_results().

See also

Other results: read_results(), render_run(), save_results()

Examples

x <- list(
  manifest = list(
    scenario = "real",
    sim = 1L,
    sims = 1L,
    data_files = data.frame(file = "main/d.csv", size = 120, mtime = 1.8e9),
    fake_real_data = FALSE,
    source_md5 = c(v01_run.R = "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210"),
    n_rows_data = 100L
  ),
  exclusions = data.frame(
    step = "age 18 or more",
    n_before = 100,
    n_excluded = 4,
    n_after = 97
  ),
  estimates = data.frame(term = "x", estimate = 1.2),
  p_interaction = 0.04
)
pbn::check_results(x)
#>                rule status
#> 1     element_names   PASS
#> 2  exclusions_table   FAIL
#> 3   allowed_objects   PASS
#> 4 no_row_per_person   PASS
#> 5 manifest_scenario   PASS
#> 6     manifest_data   PASS
#> 7   manifest_source   PASS
#>                                                                                       detail
#> 1                              manifest, and each other element with a unique syntactic name
#> 2                                          n_before - n_excluded != n_after on these rows: 1
#> 3              each element is a data.frame, an atomic vector, NULL or a plain list of these
#> 4        no data.frame has 100 rows, and no vector or matrix has 100 values in one dimension
#> 5                        the manifest names the scenario, the simulation and the simulations
#> 6 the manifest has data_files and fake_real_data for "real", or fake_md5 for a fake scenario
#> 7                                the manifest has source_md5, with the md5 of the run script
